To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

substitutions at the FG loop of the Murray Valley encephalic flavivirus MVE can alter virus entry, cell tropism, and virulence in a manner consistent with a role for glycosaminogylcans as receptors for this virus.

(i) the FG loop of MVE is important for cell entry; (ii) MVE can use glycosaminogylcans to enter cells; (iii) the FG loop is not the only receptor-binding site of MVE, and (iv) the FG loop can be used by the virus as an alternative entry site in the absence of the natural receptor(s) of MVE.
the RGD motif in the FG loop of the flavivirus E glycoprotein is involved in virus entry into cells and that the FG loop is involved in the interaction with host cell receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of virus-host interactions at the level of virus entry, a process which has been poorly investigated in the field of flavivirus pathogenesis.
the identification of the receptor-binding site of the flavivirus E glycoprotein.
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms that govern virus entry into cells and the role of virus entry for the pathogenesis of flaviviruses in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RGD motif is not essential for the entry of encephalitic viruses into mammalian cells but that it is required to ensure efficient entry and virulence in vivo.
the RGD motif of MVE does not function in cell entry and that the RGD sequence of MVE is not required for virulence.
the RGD motif in MVE E protein does not appear to be essential for virus entry, but it is required for efficient neuroinvasiveness in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FG loop in flavivirus E proteins is a functional entry determinant that can be used to manipulate the cell tropism and virulence of these viruses.
the FG loop is a multifunctional region of the flavivirus E proteins that plays a role in virus entry via interaction with glycosaminoglycerides and integrins.
the RGD motif of MVE is not required for virus entry and that it is dispensable for virulence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single amino acid change in the FG loop can result in a profound alteration of virus tropism and virulence.
the FG loop is not only important for virus entry, but it also plays an important role for virulence.
the FG loop of flavivirus E proteins is a functional receptor-binding domain that is involved in the attachment of virions to glycosaminolgyans.
